newsitem.title: UK: Irish utility buys 60,000 tonnes of Russian fuel.
newsitem.headline: Irish utility buys 60,000 tonnes of Russian fuel.

text.p: Ireland's state power company, ESB, has bought Russian fuel over the past week in anticipation of the colder winter months, sources close to the utility said on Thursday.
ESB is estimated to have purchased up to 60,000 tonnes at prices either side of $120 cif Ireland.
The fuel has been trading at a discount to high sulphur cracked because of its high water content, in excess of one percent, and because it is well supplied.
Over the last two weeks high sulphur cracked fuel, which utilities normally buy, has been breaking five year highs trading in excess of $120 delivered since October 8.
When Russian straight run fuel becomes well supplied and under price pressure it usually goes into the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp barge market.
Other utilities in the U.K or Portugual have not followed ESB's move and bought straight run, traders said.
ESB was now seen relaxed for purchases for the next few weeks.
